reason: The examples name different scars: ring-like scars at nodes (usually stipule or bud-scale scars) and French 'cicatrices foliaires' (leaf scars). One word cannot stand for all of them. PATO:0001850 scarred is a wound-tissue quality. Each statement should be annotated as absence of the scar it names.
spoon-like = shaped like a spoon, a concave 3-D shape: PATO:0002208 spoon-shaped. Not PATO:0001937 spatulate, which is a flat outline.
PATO:0002065 star shaped (EXACT synonym stellate) is defined as 'arranged like rays or radii; radiating from a common center', which is exactly the arrangement meant.

An analogy whose sense changes with the part: an erect, aerial-looking habit for a rhizome, which is itself a stem, and a terete bract that continues the culm. Like cherry-like, it has no stable meaning. Annotate the stated property instead.
stocky = short, thick and sturdy: PATO:0002310 robust ('strong, thick or sturdy'). The example 'with a thick stock' is a misreading: there 'stock' is a part (caudex), not this quality.
sub- + glaucescent (= somewhat glaucous): the value glaucous PATO:0104277 with value_qualifier approximately and the whole word as the cue, as for other 'sub-' words.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: orbicular PATO_0001934 – oblong PATO_0000946; docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md for sub-)
reason: A compound of two shape values, read as a continuum like 'linear-lanceolate'. The 'sub-' on the first value is the approximate-value pattern.

label: panduriform
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being fiddle-shaped: oblong to obovate and narrowed by a concave constriction on each side below the middle. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991024 ovate and PATO:0001937 spatulate; subpanduriform is then panduriform with value_qualifier approximately.
reason: There is no PATO or FLOPO term for panduriform, a standard shape for orchid lips and leaves. The 'sub-' word cannot be annotated until that base value exists.
sub- + pinnately compound: PATO:0000410 pinnate (leaflets on each side of a common axis) with value_qualifier approximately.
It means 'suture absent', but neither PO nor FLOPO has a fruit or sporocarp suture class, so there is no part to negate. Revisit as entity absence once a suture class exists.

target: new: conjunction of two values (dentated PATO_0001205 and ciliate)
reason: Two values that hold together on the same margin (teeth that end in cilia). This is not a continuum between them, and no single term is needed.

label: tripinnatipartite
definition: A pinnatipartite quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's primary and secondary divisions being themselves pinnatipartite, so that it is three times pinnately parted. NOTE: Modelled on FLOPO:0991159 tripinnate.
reason: There is no term for it. It is a standard degree of leaf dissection and follows the precedent of tripinnate under pinnate.
An analogy used for lamellae, folds and lines on a scar. It does not name a stable quality; the shape or colour of the line is what should be annotated.

vitreous = glassy, hard and translucent (a vitreous caryopsis). The nearest term is PATO:0001354 translucent, as in the rule for 'pellucid'. In 'glossy-vitreous' the shine is a separate value (glistening).

target: new: conjunction of two values (warty PATO_0001361 and papillose FLOPO:0991059)
reason: Moss cells bearing coarse, wart-like papillae: two surface values that hold together, not a new term.
PATO:0001885 hydrophobic is defined as 'tending to repel and not absorb water... not wetted by water'.
Leaves that shed water are not wetted by it: PATO:0001885 hydrophobic. Where a source means a shape that drains water (for example a drip tip), annotate the shape instead.

target: new: position of the greatest width
reason: It places the widest point in the lower half of the outline without fixing a shape (it covers ovate, lanceolate and deltate). It needs a 'where the maximum lies' pattern, not ovate and not a new term.
with domatia = domatia present. The FLOPO anatomy class domatium FLOPO_0986021 exists (from the previous review). 'with or without' goes to the alternatives pattern.
Moss costa with no differentiated stereid band = stereid absent in the costa (PO:0030045 stereid). 'Clearly defined' softens it, hence medium.

label: amphitropous
definition: A curved quality inhering in an ovule by virtue of the ovule's body and embryo sac being bent into a horseshoe shape, so that the micropyle lies near the funicle and the chalaza. NOTE: Botany-specific. Anatropous, orthotropous and campylotropous also have no term and would be siblings.
reason: A standard ovule orientation with no PATO or FLOPO term.
A matter of taste or horticultural appeal, not a property of the flower. Use conspicuous only where the source says showy.
Bunch-forming grasses grow in dense tufts from the base: FLOPO:0991007 caespitose (tufted, clump-forming).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (slot 1, part of the bearer): hairy PATO_0000454 on the part, white PATO_0000323 on its hairs
reason: Two statements: the part is hairy, and its hairs are white. Not canescent FLOPO:0991079, because sparse white hairs do not make the surface grey-white.
epitepalous = borne on or joined to the tepals: a relation to another part, not a term. 'Carpels epitepalous' is probably a transcription slip.

target: new: conjunction of two values (spherical PATO_0001499 and laterally compressed PATO_0002054)
reason: A globose body that is also flattened: two shape values that hold together, not a continuum. Unlike 'depressed-globose', it does not say the flattening is at the poles, so oblate does not apply.

label: heterotrichous
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's bearing two or more distinct kinds of hairs, differing in length, form or glandularity, intermixed. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991118 bearded. FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic is limited to exactly two forms.
reason: A standard indumentum term with no PATO or FLOPO term.
Inarticulate pedicels and petiolules have no joint where they separate: the negation of FLOPO:0991154 jointed.

It means 'hyalodermis absent', but there is no PO or FLOPO class for the hyalodermis (the moss stem's outer layer of enlarged hyaline cells). Add that part class first; this then becomes entity absence.

Foliose pseudoparaphyllia are leaf-like in form, as opposed to filamentous: PATO:0002457 leaf-like, as in the rule for 'foliaceous'. It is not FLOPO:0991012 leafy, which means bearing leaves. 'Narrowly' adds a width, annotated apart.
